axis: bare standing that could go either way → being held in high esteem and honor

members.tone: The good is built into the word here, so unlike *name* it needs no adjective to come out favorable.
The plainest term for what a person is held to be, carrying no verdict of its own and taking whatever *character* or disgrace is attached to it.
Treats standing as a quantity that rises and falls, and pairs it with popularity rather than the honor *reputation* names.
The full weight of the family: not merely being thought well of but being held in high esteem and honor.
Adds breadth to approval — the favor is public, where *character* keeps good standing a private matter.
The formal counterpart to *reputation*, stating the same high esteem and honor in a more elevated register.
